title: Montreal man shot by police near movie theatre identified
subtitle: Investigators have identified the Montreal man shot to death by a police officer in the parking lot of a Scarborough movie theatre earlier this week.
article: Investigators have identified the Montreal man shot to death by a police officer in the parking lot of a Scarborough movie theatre earlier this week.

34-year-old Paul Daniel was shot at after he allegedly confronted Toronto police officers outside a crowded Cineplex Odeon in Eglinton Town Centre near Eglinton and Pharmacy Aves. around 7:30 p.m. Sunday. Officers were called to the scene when a concerned citizen told police that there was a man in the parking lot holding a gun, or what looked like a gun.
Daniel was transferred to Sunnybrook Hospital where he died shortly after.

Investigators released the victim's name once family was notified Thursday morning, said Jasbir Brar, a spokeswoman for the Special Investigations Unit. An autopsy was conducted on Dec. 29, although Brar wouldn't say how many times Daniel was shot. Earlier reports suggest the victim was shot four times before he collapsed on the sidewalk.
Brar said she didn't know why Daniel was in Toronto.
"We can't speculate on what he was doing in Toronto. We're more focused on the incident," she said.

SIU is called in to investigate all cases of serious injury, death and sexual assault involving police officers. Earlier this week, the SIU said they had designated four subject officers, interviewed two witness officers and three civilian witnesses.
Brar said the investigation is ongoing and detectives are continuing to interview civilian witnesses, and sift through evidence collected at the scene.
The SIU is asking anyone who witnessed this shooting to call 416-622-1925 or 1-800-787-8529 extension No.1925.
